message: woodshed's graft (3): a streaming time stretch for looped playback at 50-100%, built as spectral::TimeStretcher.

title: TimeStretcher: output-driven, over a sample buffer, sharing time_stretch's engine
body: spectral::TimeStretcher plays a sample buffer at a speed (0.1-10x, changeable between render calls, effective from the next frame) with optional loop points, through the same private Vocoder (identity phase locking) as PitchShifter and time_stretch: one engine, three drivers. It is driven by the output: render(source, out) analyzes a frame every quarter frame of output, the cursor advancing speed * hop source samples per frame, and overlap-adds into a ring one frame ahead. Reads wrap into the loop past its end, so a frame that straddles the end holds the loop's start and the phases carry on across the seam; a pre-roll before the loop runs into it. seek() restarts phase analysis but keeps the ring, so what was playing fades out under the new frames (no click). position() is the source sample heard now (half a frame of latency after a seek). Checked: at constant speeds 1, 0.5, 2 and 0.25 the output is bit for bit time_stretch's (the same frames overlap-added in the same order), looped playback at 0.75x keeps pitch within 5 cents and level within 1 dB and the position inside the loop, a speed change mid-play keeps pitch and moves the position at the expected rate, and render / seek / set_speed never allocate (tests/no_alloc.rs). Why a buffer and not a Source or a live input: slowing a live input down needs an unbounded backlog; woodshed's use (backing tracks and recordings at 50-100%, looped for transcription) has the whole buffer. Multichannel: one stretcher per channel at the same speed and loop (their phases are independent, so a wide stereo image can blur; a linked-phase stereo version is left until someone needs it).
